name: Herdr Console
description: Inspect local Herdr workspaces and tmux sessions, read panes, send input, and receive Cindy notifications or automation triggers from Herdr events.
whenToUse: Use to inspect local Herdr agents and their panes, send prompts or input, wait for agent states, manage local Herdr and tmux panes, or bridge Herdr events into Cindy.

herdr_state.description: List Herdr workspaces, tabs, panes, and agents, including status, working directories, and titles.

herdr_read.description: Read pane or agent terminal output. Use visible for the current screen, recent for the latest lines, or recent_unwrapped for unwrapped log lines.

herdr_prompt.description: Send a prompt to a Herdr agent. With wait_until it waits for the agent to reach one of those states (idle/working/blocked/done/unknown), bounded by timeout_ms (default 120000). A target that is already blocked receives nothing. If the result is HERDR_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, read the pane first to see whether the prompt arrived.

herdr_send.description: Send text or keys to a Herdr pane (keys use Herdr key names such as enter, ctrl+h, alt+x, f1, shift+tab). If the result is HERDR_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN the request was sent but no reply arrived, so it may already have taken effect: read the pane before sending again.

herdr_wait.description: Wait for an agent to reach a state, or for pane output to match text (match like {type:"substring"|"regex", value:"text"}). A long wait runs in bounded segments under one timeout_ms budget (default 300000) and fails when that budget runs out.

herdr_control.description: Manage Herdr workspaces, tabs, panes, and Git worktrees. Close and worktree remove only when the user explicitly requests them.

herdr_notify.description: Show a notification in the Herdr terminal interface.

herdr_events.description: Manage Herdr event subscriptions: mode=status reports the current subscription, subscribe starts it (agent status changes, pane lifecycle, tab focus), unsubscribe stops it, wait blocks until one event arrives on the live subscription (match_event like {event:"pane.agent_status_changed", pane_id:"w1:p1"}; pane_id is optional).

herdr_automation_setup.description: Create a Cindy automation that only wakes on Herdr events: when an agent turns blocked or done the plugin asks the host scheduler to run it once, and the automation never runs on a timer. targetSessionId links it to an existing session. Returns the automation ID.

herdr_call.description: Call a Herdr socket API method by its full name and parameters, for the rare methods the other tools do not cover. A call can change Herdr state, including creating or closing panes and workspaces, so confirm the intent first. Method names are in the Herdr Socket API documentation.

tmux_state.description: List local tmux sessions and panes with commands, working directories, sizes, and active state. When tmux is unavailable, return available=false and a hint.

tmux_read.description: Read the screen of a tmux session/window/pane. Defaults to the visible screen; with lines, returns the last N lines (including scrollback). At most 5000 lines and about 120000 characters per call; earlier content beyond that is cut and the reply carries truncated=true with requested_lines / max_lines / char_limit. If the history is shorter, everything is returned.

tmux_send.description: Send text or keys to a tmux session / window / pane. Text is sent literally (-l), so C-b or Enter inside it are not key names; keys accepts only key names tmux recognises (Enter, Escape, F1, C-c, M-x, S-Tab) and rejects unknown names instead of typing them as text.
